coverage_notes: Verified correct (no finding): eq:reduction; Theorem thm:lean items 1-5 match the Lean sources (Lean DHL quantifies over Nat lists, which is implied by the paper's integer-tuple DHL, so the stated implications hold in the direction used); all 65 tuples admissible with the stated diameters; Thm thm:Mk0 values are truncations of the stored exact quotients (4.0020697619, 4.0027134339, 2.0041054153); 'least k' claims 105/102/102, 64, 58, 56 confirmed by reruns at k-1 (3.99868, 3.99484, 3.99716; cert_M55_D18e 3.99153); 3.99931 at k=101, d=19 confirmed, and d=23 gives 3.999325, so 'polynomials in P1,P2 alone stop at k=102' is well supported; Lemma lem:egf and its proof are correct (E_k(b) = sum of multinomial b!/prod c^i! times prod w(c^i)!, a positive integer); the inner-integral and the three eps identities are correct; the inverse-iteration shift argument is valid for the plain simplex; Thm thm:Mk values (except provenance of M_105, F003) are truncations of stored certificates; Thm thm:Meps basis sizes, and the agreement with Polymath8b's printed digits, hold; Table tab:eps entries match the jsonl data up to the rounding issue in F001; Prop prop:rigid: the perfect-graph step (STAB = QSTAB for the perfect complement, so P = conv of clique indicators), convexity, the slicing exponents and the monotonicity are all correct; Prop prop:rigid-eps: the mu-rescaling, the region inclusion (equivalent to -|u|(1+eps) <= -|u|(1-eps)), the j=1 Cauchy-Schwarz value 1+eps, the embedding limit (the region radius tends to 1-eps from below, so the limit holds by monotone convergence) and the equality for a largest clique all hold; degenerate omega=1 makes both criteria unsatisfiable, consistently; GEH condition eps<1/(k-1) is weaker for omega<=k. Not checked: Lean build/axiom output (reading only, per instructions); external-literature citation numbers (Maynard Prop 4.2, Pol14b Thm 3.9/3.12/3.13, section 7.2) were not checked against sources (no internet); degree-25/27 certificates not rebuilt (16-53 min builds).

findings.title: Stated certified lower bounds rounded up past the certified value (Thm thm:Meps, Table tab:eps, eps k=3 table)
findings.location: Theorem thm:Meps, paper/main.tex:403; also Table tab:eps lines 441-445, Remark table lines 571-574, theta table line 356
findings.claim: M_{50,1/25} >= 4.0012466 (degree 25) and >= 4.0043063 (degree 27), certified in exact arithmetic.
findings.issue: The exact Rayleigh quotients stored in code/cert_M50e25_D25e.json and code/cert_M50e25_D27e.json are 4.001246593441... and 4.004306258353.... Both stated bounds exceed these (4.0012466 > 4.00124659344; 4.0043063 > 4.00430625835), so neither inequality as printed is what the certificates prove; they are round-to-nearest, not truncations. The same convention appears in Table tab:eps, captioned 'Certified lower bounds': e.g. k=49, eps=1/50, D=18 printed 3.95066 vs 3.950655280 in runs/scan_k49.jsonl; eps=1/30, D=18 3.95745 vs 3.957446343; eps=0, D=18 3.90102 vs 3.901015520; eps=1/50, D=16 3.93491 vs 3.934909829; eps=1/20, D=16 3.92741 vs 3.927408074; eps=1/20, D=20 3.96244 vs 3.962437041; k=50, D=20: eps=1/30 3.98522 vs 3.985219018, eps=1/25 3.98395 vs 3.983945393, eps=1/20 3.97745 vs 3.977447280. (The k=50, D=16 column is truncated, so the table even mixes the two conventions.) The eps remark table at line 571-574 does the same: 1.518567 vs 1.518566714, 1.482143 vs 1.482142652, 1.264698 vs 1.264697853, 1.882282 vs 1.882281975, 1.717104 vs 1.717103517 (notes/enlarged_pigeonhole_d5_d10.txt). In the theta table, the necessary thresholds 2(k-1)/(k log k) = 0.51372, 0.52862, 0.54646, 0.78173 are printed as 0.514, 0.529, 0.547, 0.782, i.e. slightly stronger than what the bound gives. Thm thm:Mk0 and thm:Mk use truncation correctly. No conclusion (>4 or <4) changes.
findings.analysis: Exact check: Fraction(cert['rayleigh']) >= Fraction('4.0012466') is False and >= Fraction('4.0043063') is False. The values remain >4 by a wide margin, so Cor cor:246 is unaffected.
findings.suggested_fix: Print truncated (rounded-down) digits for every quantity labelled a certified lower bound: 4.0012465 and 4.0043062 in thm:Meps; truncate Table tab:eps and the eps k=3 table entries, or state that entries are rounded to nearest; round the theta thresholds down (0.513, 0.528, 0.546, 0.781) or print them as approximations.

findings.title: 'Best that the plain simplex gives' is not justified by the cited bound, which leaves k = 51, 52, 53 open
findings.location: Section 'The sieve constant, with exact certificates', paper/main.tex:341-343, with the justification at lines 347-349
findings.quote: is the best that the plain simplex gives with Bombieri--Vinogradov (see the
findings.claim: Corollary cor:578 (H_1 <= 270, k = 54) is the best that the plain simplex gives with BV, as shown in the next subsection.
findings.issue: The next subsection proves only that M_k > 4 forces k >= 51, from M_k <= k/(k-1) log k (equal to 3.99186 at k=50 and 4.01046 at k=51). It does not exclude M_51, M_52 or M_53 > 4, which would give H_1 <= H(51)=252, H(52)=254 or H(53)=264 on the plain simplex, all below 270. The paper elsewhere says exactly this ('shows where the method stops (k>=51)', lines 591-592 and 1753-1754), so the sentence at 341-343 contradicts the paper's own stated limit. What is established is that k=54 is the best this project (and Polymath8b) has certified on the plain simplex, and that k <= 50 is impossible.
findings.analysis: Recomputed k/(k-1) log k at k=50 and k=51. No statement in full-source.tex gives an upper bound M_53 <= 4 or similar (searched for M_{51}, M_{52}, M_{53}, k=53).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: 'Corollary cor:578 is the best certified on the plain simplex with BV (by Polymath8b and by us); the dual bound of the next subsection shows only that k <= 50 is impossible there, so k = 51, 52, 53 remain open for this method.' Alternatively cite an actual upper bound showing M_53 < 4, if one exists.

findings.title: M_105 >= 4.17427 (all symmetric, degree 11) and the k=50, D=16 column of Table tab:eps have no stored certificate or data file
findings.location: Theorem thm:Mk, paper/main.tex:305; text at lines 299-301; Table tab:eps caption line 433
findings.claim: M_105 >= 4.17427 is Computed in exact rational arithmetic, and code/verify_cert.py re-evaluates each stored coefficient vector exactly.
findings.issue: code/ contains certificates for every other value of thm:Mk (cert_M64_D12, cert_M58_D16e, cert_M56_D18e, cert_M55_D20e, cert_M54_D23e), but none for M_105 at degree 11 with 195 coefficients: code/cert_M105.json is the 42-coefficient P1,P2 vector of thm:Mk0 (quotient 4.0020697619), and code/scan_results.json has only the P1,P2 runs. The value appears only as text in status.json:176. So the sentence 'rebuilds both Gram matrices from scratch and re-evaluates each stored coefficient vector' does not cover this entry. Similarly, the k=50, D=16 column of Table tab:eps is attributed to 'direct runs of code/mk_general.py' with no data file in runs/ or code/. The values themselves are correct: rerunning 'mk_general.py 105 11' gives n=195, exact quotient 4.174272850696 (13 s), and 'mk_general.py 50 16 --even --eps e' gives 3.901734, 3.949799, 3.950417 for e = 0, 1/50, 1/25, matching the table.
findings.analysis: Searched every JSON under the repository (outside referee/) for k=105 records: only cert_M105.json (D=11, 42 coefficients) and scan_results.json (n=42).
findings.suggested_fix: Store code/cert_M105_D11.json (mk_general.py 105 11 --cert ..., about 15 s) and a small runs/ file for the k=50, D=16 column, or say in the text that this value is recorded without a stored vector.

findings.title: k=3 consistency remark does not state the shifts and D, so the bound it checks against (M_2) is not determined
findings.location: Remark [Computed, consistency check for k=3], paper/main.tex:506-511 (also the eps remark, lines 563-579)
findings.quote: $M_2=1/(1-W(1/e))=1.3859\ldots$\,. The half-weighted functional is far below
findings.claim: The lower bounds for M_3[c] at c=(1,1,0) and (1/2,1,1/2) lie below M_2, as Proposition prop:rigid requires.
findings.issue: Proposition prop:rigid bounds M_k[c] by alpha_D(c) M_omega, and both alpha_D and omega depend on the shifts and on D, which the remark never fixes. The comparison with M_2 is the right one only when h_2-h_1 <= D, h_3-h_2 <= D and h_3-h_1 > D (path graph: omega=2, alpha_D((1/2,1,1/2)) = alpha_D((1,1,0)) = 1). For D below both gaps, omega=1 and alpha_D((1/2,1,1/2))=2, so the proposition requires only M_3[c] <= 2; for D >= h_3-h_1 the bound is M_3. The intended configuration (shifts (0,1,2), D=1) is stated only in code/enlarged_pigeonhole.py and notes/enlarged-rigidity.md. The numbers themselves reproduce (weighted_pigeonhole.py degree 6: 1.646438, 1.357924, 1.160439).
findings.analysis: Worked out alpha_D and omega for the three possible graph types on 3 points.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'for the shifts (0,1,2) and D=1, so that omega=2 and alpha_D(c)=1 for both weight vectors' to the k=3 remark and to the eps remark.

findings.title: Abstract's 'every statement carries a label' is not met by the two end-to-end corollaries
findings.location: Abstract, paper/main.tex:69-72; Corollaries cor:578 (line 330) and cor:246 (line 418)
findings.quote: directions that later versions will test. Every statement carries one of the
findings.claim: Every statement carries one of the labels Lean-checked, Computed, Proved here, Literature, Claimed, Open.
findings.issue: Corollaries cor:578 and cor:246 carry only '[end-to-end within this project]', with no status label, though they are exactly the statements where the status is mixed (Computed + Lean-checked + Literature inputs). Lemma lem:egf has no label in its header; its status ('Proved here; possibly folklore') is only in the sentence before it. Equation eq:reduction and the bound M_k <= k/(k-1) log k at line 347 also have no label (the latter is attributed to Polymath8b, so Literature is implied).
findings.analysis: Checked every theorem-like environment in units 002-004 for a \lbl{...} tag.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the corollaries, e.g. '[Computed + Lean-checked, conditional on Literature inputs]', put '\lbl{Proved here}' in the header of lem:egf, and mark eq:reduction and the dual bound as Literature (or weaken the abstract sentence to 'every result').
